Subject: Renewal coming up — request to double reserved GPUs and update commit

Hi Grace,

Our renewal for the dedicated pool is coming up on June 1. Over the last quarter our latency-sensitive traffic has increased and we think moving from an 8-GPU reserved pool to 16 would be the safest way to meet peak QPS and avoid throttling during our nightly batch runs.

Can you share: 1) a commercial estimate for increasing the reserved pool 8→16 starting at renewal, 2) recommended monthly commit change to keep unit cost reasonable (we're currently on a committed 12k token-equivalent per month), and 3) any SLA/throughput guarantees you can offer for the larger pool?

We also want to understand activation timing — ideally a phased ramp rather than an all-at-once change so we can validate performance.

Thanks,
Sophie

Subject: Draft sizing + throughput SLO for 16-GPU reserved pool (for review)

Grace / Ben / Sophie — following the call yesterday, here's a concise technical recommendation. I've attached a spreadsheet with modeled latency and token-cost assumptions.

Summary recommendation:
- Reserved pool size: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool).
- Target steady-state throughput SLO: 450 tokens/sec sustained per GPU (aggregated 7,200 tokens/sec).
- Burst handling: automatic 30% burst buffer via autoscaling to handle nightly batch spikes up to ~9,400 tokens/sec for up to 20 minutes.
- KV/prefix caching enabled with a 48-hour cache TTL — expected to reduce token compute by ~18% for your conversational workload.

Commercial implication (high level):
- Suggested monthly commit: increase from your current "12k token-equivalent" to 22k token-equivalent to preserve cost-per-token while covering the higher steady-state utilization.
- If Atlas prefers a phased commitment, we can do a 60/40 split month 1/month 2 where the full 16 GPUs are reserved but the committed billing ramps to 22k over 2 months.

I've attached: Redwood_Throughput_SLA_Draft_20260515.xlsx (SLO language + metrics), and a preliminary estimate in the sheet. Ben, can you convert this into a commercial proposal and order form?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
